recipe: Greek baked salmon with butter beans, tomatoes & feta
servesNote: 2 portions — Karl 1, Maria dinner plus next-day lunch. 890 kcal / 51 g protein each. ⭐ The beans do three jobs: carb, a third of the protein, and they catch the salmon fat and tomato juice so nothing is wasted.
adaptations: ✅ THE SALMON IS IN THE HOUSE — Tuesday bought two 2-packs. The butter beans, olives, feta, baby plum tomatoes and parsley are not.
⚠️ THE TOMATO PASTE SACHET IS OUT — 1 tbsp of the tomato double concentrate from the tube, squeezed straight into the tin at step 1. It only ever gets tossed through here, so the swap is clean.

⭐ VINE TOMATOES ARE IN THE HOUSE instead of baby plum. They will not burst the same way — halve them all rather than leaving half whole, and expect more juice and less pop. A drained tin of cherry tomatoes is the recipe's own stated fallback: you lose the burst and keep the sauce.
⭐ CANNELLINI OR HARICOT WORK IDENTICALLY if butter beans are not on the shelf.
⚠️ 120 g ALDI FILLETS ARE THINNER than the 170 g American ones most recipes are timed for. Err early at step 6 — this is where dry chalky salmon comes from.

equipment.item: A roasting tin big enough for one rough layer
equipment.why: ⛔ crowded beans steam instead of colouring
⭐ 1 tbsp salt in ~400 ml cold water — this is what stops the white curd
patting the salmon very dry after the brine

prep: Oven to 200°C fan / 220°C conventional, shelf in the upper-middle third.

⭐ BRINE THE SALMON WHILE THE OVEN HEATS. Dissolve 1 tbsp salt in ~400 ml cold water, slide the fillets in, leave 10–15 minutes. Not fussiness: it firms the outer layer so far less white albumin weeps out, and it seasons the flesh through rather than just the surface.

steps.text: Tip the beans, onion, garlic, all the tomatoes and olives into the roasting tin. Squeeze in the tomato concentrate, add 1½ tbsp oil, oregano, Greek herbs, the pinch of cinnamon, pepper and 2 tbsp water. Toss with your hands until every bean is slicked and faintly orange.

Roast until the tomato skins have split and slumped, the onion wedges are floppy with browned tips, and the beans sitting proudest have gone matte and slightly crusted. Splash in more water and shake if it looks dry.
Lift the salmon from the brine and pat it VERY dry both sides — a wet surface steams rather than colours. Rub the skin with a little oil and a pinch of Maldon.
Stir the beans, push them aside to make two hollows, and settle the salmon in skin-side up, sitting ON the beans rather than in the juices.

Roast until the thickest part turns from glassy-translucent to matte-opaque and the flakes separate cleanly under a fork tip with a little resistance. A thin knife held in the centre five seconds should come out just warm against your lip. ⚠️ Err early — it carries on cooking in the tin.
⭐ Stand 5 minutes, undisturbed. The fish finishes on residual heat and the bean juices thicken.
Crumble the feta over the beans and tomatoes — ⛔ around the salmon, not on it, so the fish stays fish. Scatter the lemon zest.

⭐ Squeeze over the juice of half the lemon, then trickle the last of the oil over RAW. Do both. Ten sources roast salmon perfectly well and then serve it flat; the raw oil and the acid are what make the tin taste seasoned rather than merely cooked.

Parsley, a last pinch of Maldon on the skin, serve from the tin with lemon wedges. ⭐ Maria's next-day lunch: excellent, and better COLD than reheated. ⛔ Do not reheat the salmon — it overcooks and the albumin comes back. Flake it through the beans cold with a fresh squeeze of lemon and a trickle of oil; the feta and tomato juices soak into the beans overnight, which is a gain.
